Done. I picked up the handoff's ranked list, worked all three, and two of the three findings contradicted what that list predicted.

**1. Strip reference sections → done, but the plan was aimed one layer too shallow (PR #13)**

Stripping the bibliography alone changes *nothing* — the citation band stays at 37. The band is the **49 in-text `[n]` markers** scattered through pages 2–7, which supply every integer 1..30 by themselves. Strip those too and it falls to **4**. Anyone implementing the plan literally would have measured zero improvement and concluded the idea was wrong.

Narrowing the band nearly shipped this verifier's first false alarm: the paper writes *"Seven coronal plane angles"* (the word, 4×) and the digit `7` appears nowhere in its body, so a truthful "7 angles" deck would have been called fabricated. Number-word matching prevents that.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| citation band | 37 | **4** |
| planted numeric defects caught | 5 of 6 | **6 of 6** |
| false alarms on review 001's 67 real claims | 0 | **0** |
| API calls to establish it | — | **0** |

**2. What wrote `perch.duckdb` → answered, and the record was five months stale (`_INBOX` PR #1)**

Not 2026-04-30 — last written **2026-09-19**, 13,346 rows through `test_date 2026-09-18`. It can't have come from git (untracked, gitignored, last fetch was a day *earlier*), the credential is here, and the `.bat`'s Perch step is still enabled — only GPS was disabled. **Windows is already a Perch writer**, so the decision open since 09-13 was resting on a false premise. The half I can't answer from here — whether the Mac writes it too — is recorded with the two commands to run there.

**3. `semantic_find` → blocked on corpus, not effort**

No Kitman or MyLink contract, quote or pricing document exists in `~/DEV`, on Drive (full depth, 9 filename patterns), or in personal Gmail; the vault is Mac-only and the NCAA charter isn't on disk either. The likely location is **Baylor Outlook**, which isn't connected to this session. I deliberately did *not* substitute a different document and call the capability proven.

Two corrections worth flagging: a reviewer caught that my running-header strip was a **silent no-op** — no test failed, because the band is 4 either way; what exposed it was the byte count not reconciling (29,871 where the table predicted 28,953). entries.name: ExitWorktree
entries.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

action.description: "keep" leaves the worktree and branch on disk; "remove" deletes both.

discard_changes.description: Required true when action is "remove" and the worktree has uncommitted files or unmerged commits. The tool will refuse and list them otherwise.

lines: +# 2026-09-20 (third) — the apparatus strip, and Perch's writer identified
+Third handoff for 2026-09-20. Picks up the ranked list from
+`2026-09-20-prose-numbers-and-jev-scoping.md` and works its top three. Two are
+delivered, one is blocked on something that does not exist on this box.
+**Two of the three findings contradict what the previous handoff said to expect.**
+That is the useful part of this document.
+## 1. Strip reference sections — DONE, and the plan was aimed one layer too shallow
+PR **#13**, branch `worktree-strip-reference-apparatus`. Full write-up in
+`docs/DELIVERABLE_VERIFIER.md` under *Stripping the apparatus*.
+The plan said: strip reference sections from page text before matching. **Measured,
+that alone changes nothing.**
+| text the check reads | citation band | chars |
+| raw pages (before) | **37** | 38,456 |
+| bibliography removed | **37** | 30,062 |
+| bibliography + in-text `[n]` markers removed | **4** | 29,871 |
+| + running header removed | **4** | 28,953 |
+The band is the **in-text markers**, not the bibliography — 49 of them across pages
+2–7 (`[1-3]`, `[26, 30]`, `[27]`), supplying every integer 1..30 by themselves.
+Implementing the plan literally, re-running, and measuring zero improvement was the
+likely outcome, and it would have looked like the idea was wrong. It was not wrong,
+it was one layer too shallow.
+`docs/STATUS.md` and `DELIVERABLE_VERIFIER.md` both asserted the band "is the
+bibliography". Both now carry the correction, with the wrong sentence kept visible
+rather than quietly edited, so the shallow fix does not get re-derived.
+### The false alarm this nearly shipped
+Narrowing the band is what makes small integers checkable, and that is the dangerous
+half. Paper 001 writes **"Seven coronal plane angles"** — the word, four times — and
+the digit `7` appears **nowhere** in its body. A deck truthfully saying "7 angles"
+would have been reported **fabricated**: the first false alarm on a tool whose whole
+value is having none.
+`source.find_number_word` matches spelled-out integers; a figure is absent only when
+**neither** the digits nor the word appear. `find_number` and `find_number_rounded`
+are untouched — still two rules, still on purpose.
+A second trap, found by running the matcher rather than by thinking about it: the
+page extractor leaves a soft hyphen at every line-break hyphenation, so "tenderness"
+arrives as `ten<U+00AD> derness` and a bare `\bten\b` matches inside it — finding the
+number word "ten" in a paper that never uses it. `source.dehyphenate` rejoins first.
+### Result
+| | before | after |
+| citation band, paper 001 | 37 | **4** |
+| planted numeric defects caught deterministically | 5 of 6 | **6 of 6** |
+| false alarms on review 001's 67 real claims | 0 | **0** |
+| API calls to establish any of it | — | **0** |
+`num3` was the documented miss and is now caught. Both numbers come from running the
+pre-check over `calibrate.PLANTED` itself and over review 001's real claims, not from
+transcribing them.
+`body_pages()` feeds the **numeric presence checks only**. The model path still reads
+full pages, so its measured false-alarm behaviour is undisturbed; the table path is
+unchanged.
+Free suites grew with the cases that would have caught both traps:
+`verify.py --selftest` 10 → 12, `source.py --self-test` 7 → 15. Still no key, no
+network.
+## 2. What wrote `perch.duckdb` — ANSWERED. Windows did, and it is not stale
+`_INBOX` PR **#1**, branch `perch-writer-verified`. The ownership question has been
+open since 09-13 **on a false premise.**
+| | recorded | verified 2026-09-20 |
+| rows | — | **13,346** (April's ingest left 12,300) |
+Real new data, not a touched mtime. And it **cannot have arrived by sync**: the file
+is untracked and gitignored, `dev-sync` moves work through GitHub only and never
+transports ignored files, the repo's last fetch was 09-18 (a day *before* the write),
+and every other gitignored file in that repo still dates from March/April. Only this
+one moved.
+The credential is present, `src/perch_ingest.py` runs against the live API, and
+**step 3 of `refresh_all_data.bat` is still enabled** — only the GPS step was REM'd.
+**So this was never a decision about whether to make Windows a writer. It already is
+one.** That reframes the question the decision was written to answer.
+The 11:47 AM write was **not** the scheduled run: `\Refresh_All_Data` last ran 09-19
+**8:45:50 PM** and returned `2147946720` (`0x800710E0`) — the same non-zero code
+`DailyGmailDigest` returns, the sleep/power signature already recorded for
+DailyBackup. Single daily 8:00 PM trigger, no repetition, no catch-up. So the morning
+write was an ad-hoc run by hand, most likely the "run the `.bat` once by hand" step
+already sitting under Next.
+**Still open, and it needs the Mac.** Whether that box writes Perch too. No Perch
+launchd plist exists in any repo here (only `com.keystone.gpspull`, which is GPS) —
+but the Mac keeps its **own gitignored copy**, so two caches can drift without either
+machine ever seeing a conflict. That is exactly the GPS failure shape. Run there:
+ls -l ~/DEV/PlayerProfiles_FB_03-28-2026/data/perch.duckdb
+launchctl list | grep -i perch
+Recommendation, Eric's call: **name Windows the Perch owner** and say so in the
+`.bat`, mirroring the GPS comment block already in that file. If the Mac is writing
+too, REM the Mac's side rather than Windows' — Windows holds the working credential,
+the scheduled task and the fresh database.
+`forceplate.db` is a **separate** question and **is** genuinely stale (2026-08-02,
+ingest broken). Flagged in the PR so this correction is not carried over to it.
+## 3. `semantic_find` on the Kitman / MyLink contracts — BLOCKED, no corpus
+**The documents do not exist on this machine.** Searched, all zero hits for a
+contract, quote or pricing document:
+- `~/DEV`, full depth — only `_INBOX/Kitman_Labs_API_Reference.md` (an API doc, not a
+  contract) and two 2025 Kitman injury-data exports.
+- `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive`, full depth, on `mylink`, `my link`,
+  `kitman`, `quote`, `pricing`, `proposal`, `renewal`, `SOW`, `agreement` — **no
+  MyLink document of any kind**, and nothing resembling a Kitman contract.
+- `~/SecondBrain` — **does not exist on Windows** (the vault is Mac-only; already an
+  open item in `_INBOX/docs/STATUS.md`). If a vendor demo call was synced from
+  Fireflies, it is on the Mac.
+- The NCAA charter the previous handoff named as an alternate corpus is **also not on
+  disk** — the only NCAA hits are research PDFs and an attestations document.
+- **Gmail** (`eric.rash11@gmail.com`, connector attached, read-only search on
+  `MyLink OR Kitman OR "Kitman Labs"`, ~35 threads): all marketing from
+  `info@kitmanlabs.com`, a 2025 job application, and Morning Briefing mail. **No
+  quote, contract or pricing thread, and no MyLink thread at all.**
+**The likely reason, and it points somewhere specific.** The connected mailbox is the
+*personal* account. Baylor vendor correspondence goes to `eric_rash@baylor.edu`, which
+is Outlook and is **not connected to this session**. That is where a Kitman renewal or
+a MyLink quote would be. So the corpus is probably not missing, just not reachable
+from here.
+So `semantic_find` is not blocked on build effort, it is blocked on input. Do not
+substitute a different document and call the capability proven; the question it is
+meant to feed is Kitman-vs-MyLink pricing, and that needs those documents.
+**Two ways to unblock, both Eric's:**
+1. Pull the Kitman and MyLink quotes out of **Baylor Outlook** and drop them on Drive.
+   Personal Gmail has already been searched and does not have them.
+2. Or build `semantic_find` against a vendor agreement that **does** exist —
+   `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\05_SYSTEMS\Hawkin\HDI SAAS Agreement 12.25.docx`
+   is the same document shape (vendor SaaS terms, plain questions about what it
+   permits). That proves the capability now and leaves the Kitman question waiting on
+   its own inputs. It does **not** answer Kitman-vs-MyLink.
+The cookbook design from the previous handoff still stands and is unaffected: Choice
+over tagged line IDs plus a Noul asking whether an answer exists at all, cap 255 lines
+per request.
+## Next actions, most important first
+1. **Merge PR #13** (TypeSafe) and **`_INBOX` PR #1**. Both are self-contained; #1 is
+   record-only and touches no code, schedule or database.
+2. **Run the two Mac commands above** and settle Perch ownership. It is the only half
+   of that question this box cannot answer, and until it is answered the drift may be
+   live.
+3. **Decide the `semantic_find` corpus** — find the real contracts, or approve the
+   Hawkin agreement as a stand-in to prove the capability.
+4. Unchanged from the previous handoff: Weekly_Research_Review PRs **#7** and **#8**
+   still need a decision (#8 carries **DO NOT SEND**); the 25 junk Zotero records and
+   the 4 TOS papers still need a write-access key; Mac enablement of the router and
+   Zotero bridge.
+## Gotchas carried forward, plus three new ones
+- **NEW: "strip the references" is the wrong instruction for this class of problem.**
+  Strip the *apparatus* — bibliography, in-text markers, running headers. Measure the
+  band after each, because the one that sounds most important moved it by zero.
+- **NEW: the page extractor leaves soft hyphens (U+00AD) at line-break
+  hyphenations.** Any word-level search over page text must de-hyphenate first, or
+  "ten" is found inside "tenderness".
+- **NEW: a strip that removes nothing passes every test.** The first running-header
+  finder anchored its common prefix on page 1, but a title page carries extra
+  furniture ahead of the banner (`RESEARCH | Article in Press …` vs
+  `Article in Press …`), so the prefix came back empty and it stripped nothing —
+  while three documents said it did. No suite failed, because the band is 4 either
+  way. What caught it was the **byte count not reconciling**: the regression printed
+  `body 29,871`, the refs-plus-markers figure, where the header row predicted 28,953.
+  When a step is supposed to remove something, assert on how much it removed, not
+  only on the headline metric.
+- **NEW: `2147946720` / `0x800710E0` on a Windows scheduled task is the sleep/power
+  signature**, not a script failure — the same shape as the DailyBackup
+  `3221225786` note. Two custom tasks here return it. Check the artefact's modified
+  time before concluding a job did not run.
+- **`.env` existence can be checked without reading it.** A credential probe that
+  greps the file's contents trips the sandbox's credential guard, and rightly. `ls`
+  plus `git status --ignored` answers "does this box hold the key" with no secret in
+  scope.
+- `verify.py --selftest` and `source.py --self-test` are free; `test_verify.py` costs
+  live calls. Run the free ones while iterating — this session's whole result was
+  established with zero API calls.
+- Two number-matching rules on purpose. Merging them ships a misquote.
+- On Windows `git worktree remove` fails with Permission denied; `rm -rf` the
+  directory then the matching `.git/worktrees/` entry.
+- A Git Bash path (`/g/My Drive/...`) is not openable by Python; use `G:\My Drive\...`.

content.content:
## What this unlocks that we cannot do today

Four of these are genuinely new capability, not a cheaper version of something we have.

**1. Free text becomes model features.** The autoresearch cookbook turns 2,000 wine
tasting notes into 67 numeric columns and trains CatBoost on them. Held-out RMSE went
from 3.09 (predict the mean) to 2.47 (word counts) to 2.15 (just ask Jev for the score)
to **1.77** (38 decomposed feature questions). The decomposition beat asking directly,
which is the whole thesis. Our equivalent: coach notes, wellness comments, RTP
narrative, and scouting text become inputs to a model instead of prose nobody scores.
Start on CFB scouting or public text, which is tier A. Athlete narrative is tier B or C
and waits.

**2. ~~Athlete ID reconciliation without a threshold to fit.~~ WITHDRAWN 2026-09-20 —
measured, and there is no problem here to solve.** ~~We have the same name spelled four
ways across Catapult, VALD, Perch, S2, and the roster, and today that is
hand-matching.~~ The entity-alignment recipe makes the three Score levels *be* the three
actions (leave unlinked, send to a curator, merge), so there is no number to tune, and
rides three Nouls along in the same request to tell the curator which field disagrees.
On 450 pairs it settled 89% automatically and queued 11%. Athlete names are PII, so
this is tier B and needs a de-identified key mapping first.

> **What the measurement found** (`athlete_matching/measure_residue.py`, full write-up
> in `ATHLETE_KEY_MAPPING.md`):
>
> - The premise above is **false**. The name is not "spelled four ways": of the 300
>   athletes that found any counterpart above 80, **287 settle on exact normalised
=== SEQUENCE ===
## Sequence

**First: the skill router.** It pays off across all 23 projects rather than one, and the
fit question I flagged on 09-19 is now resolved: 182 skills render to 16,089 characters,
about 4k tokens, so our ~155 fit inside the 32k budget with room to spare. Measured on
488 requests against Haiku 4.5, wrong skill loads fell 16.8% to 7.3% and needless loads
9.8% to 4.0%. It fixed 37 requests and broke 7.

Design constraints that are not optional here:

- It runs as a `UserPromptSubmit` hook, which means a network call on **every** prompt.
  Our memsearch hook is currently failing with `ETIMEDOUT` 8x consecutively. Same
  fragility class.
- Therefore: hard timeout around 2 seconds, **fail open** (no suggestion, never a
  blocked prompt), and no retries in the hot path.
- Use the cookbook's exact wording, including "Ignore this if it does not fit what the
  user actually asked for." Pushing harder wins compliance on wrong suggestions too.
- Patch both `.claude/hooks/` and `.codex/hooks/`, and run it under the shell the
  MSYS-stall fix settled on, not Git Bash.

**Next two, in order:** Zotero backlog classification with confidence backoff (tier A,
small, and the 1,018-papers-for-$0.08 demo is literally the same job), then the
deliverable verifier on the status report and Research in 5.

**Next two, in order:** Zotero backlog classification with confidence backoff (tier A,
small, and the 1,018-papers-for-$0.08 demo is literally the same job), then the

## Re-ranked 2026-09-20, after five items were resolved

All three of the original sequence shipped. Five of fourteen rows are now closed:
`skill_suggestion` (live), `classification_using_confidence` (1,418 records),
`citation_check` (live and gating, 6 of 6 after the apparatus strip),
`entity_alignment` (**withdrawn**, measured) and PP_Recruiting screening (**rejected**).

### The rule this project earned, stated as a gate rather than a story

Every item that was measured moved, and every one moved *down*. Entity alignment was
ranked second and was withdrawn. PP_Recruiting offered two obvious fits that both
collapsed into code. The Zotero renames were recommended skip. `AUTO_ACCEPT` came in
at the cookbook's 0.90 and measured to 0.80; the Zotero cutoff came in at 0.90 and
measured to 0.50. That is not bad luck, it is a missing gate. **Build only where all
three hold:**

1. **The answer is genuinely fuzzy** — not a join, not a threshold, not a lookup.
2. **Something already consumes the answer.** No consumer, no build. This is the
   Zotero-renames test.
3. **A code baseline was measured first.** If deterministic code gets most of the way,
   the model is decoration.

Each withdrawn item failed a *different* one of these, which is why no single check
would have caught them. Entity alignment failed (1) — exact string equality settled
287 of 300 and fuzzy matching contributed zero settled pairs. The Zotero renames
failed (2). The prose-number work nearly failed (3) and was saved only because the
band was measured before and after.

### Next three

**1. `sde_cascade` — but scoped, and the scoping is the deliverable.**
The target surface is real and large: **126 `STATUS.md` files and 79 handoffs** in
`~/DEV`. The failure is live — on 2026-09-20 three documents asserted the running
header was stripped when it removed nothing, and this very file's sibling asserted
the citation band "is the bibliography", which aimed the session's top-priority task
one layer too shallow.

But "verify our state claims" is a category, not a build, and as a category it has
exactly the smell that got entity alignment withdrawn. Sort the claims first:

| claim shape | example from 09-20 | who checks it |
|---|---|---|
| a date, count, path, or "does X exist" | "`perch.duckdb` last written 2026-04-30" | **code** — `stat`, `git`, a byte count |
| a step's effect | "the running header is stripped" | **code** — assert `chars_removed > 0` |
| prose about what a linked document says | "PRs #7 and #8 are not merged"; "`run_pipeline.py` exists" | **Jev** — this is `citation_check`'s exact shape |
| a causal claim | "the band *is* the bibliography" | **neither** — needs a controlled measurement |

So the honest first step is not code, it is an **inventory**: take ten handoffs,
classify every claim into those four rows, and count. If the Jev-shaped row is under
about a quarter, `sde_cascade` is a code linter that needs no model, and should be
built as one. Same pattern as `measure_residue.py` — measure the residue, let the
number decide. **Do that inventory before writing any Jev call.**

**2. `rerank_typesafe` — second because it is the one that can be measured cheaply.**
memsearch is rung L1 of the retrieval ladder in `memory-write`, hit on every "did we
already…?", against a haystack of 126 STATUS files, 79 handoffs, ~230 compiled
articles and the daily logs. One Noul per query-candidate pair, tier A, small.

Pre-register the test before building: pull **ten real past questions** from the
transcripts, record whether the right answer is in the current top-5, and only build
if it is not. If the hit rate is already 9 of 10, reranking buys nothing and this is
the Zotero-renames trap wearing a different hat.

**3. `composite-scoring` — possible, with the caveat stated up front.**
The consumer is real (`project-triage/slate.py`, with tests; the slate is capped at 5
and full). But the obvious test — does Jev's ordering match Eric's? — **proves
nothing on five items**, where chance agreement is high, and the slate is Eric's
call by design rather than a bottleneck. Either find a bigger ranking surface (the
full project registry, not the slate) or accept it as low-value and skip it. Do not
run the five-item comparison and treat agreement as validation.

### Blocked on access, not on effort — and both share one unblock

- **`semantic_find`**: no Kitman or MyLink contract, quote or pricing document exists
  in `~/DEV`, on Drive (full depth, nine filename patterns), or in personal Gmail;
  the vault is Mac-only. The documents are almost certainly in **Baylor Outlook**,
  which is not connected.
- **`autoresearch_feature_discovery`**: the biggest genuine upside on this map
  (decomposition beat asking directly, RMSE 1.77 against 2.15) and governance is no
  longer the gate — but **there is no input corpus on this box.** Checked the Kitman
  injury export: 29 columns, and the only long fields are `Pathology`, which is a
  controlled clinical vocabulary rather than prose, and `Game Opposition`, which is
  team names. No narrative column at all. That is the PP_Recruiting finding repeating.

Both need access to a system that holds the prose — Kitman's narrative fields behind a
key that is not read-only, or Baylor Outlook. **One access conversation unblocks two
items**, which makes it worth more than either alone.

### Demoted on inspection

**`function_calling`** reads better on the map than it is. Claude Code already *is*
the natural-language-to-CLI layer, so routing a chat request through Jev adds a step
where a working one exists. The one place it is not redundant is the same place the
skill router paid off: **as a hook**, deciding without a conversation turn. Build it
only in that form, or not at all.

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. browser-use <<'PY'

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""How many handoff claims are actually Jev-shaped? Measure it before building.

`sde_cascade` sits at the top of the capability map's re-ranked list, and the map
pre-registered the question rather than the answer: *most* of what a handoff asserts
looks like a date, a count, a path or a test result, and code checks those. Only a
claim about what some OTHER document says has the shape `citation_check` already
proves. So the thing worth measuring first is the mix.

**Pre-registered decision rule** (written into `JEV_CAPABILITY_MAP.md` before this
script existed): if the Jev-shaped share of checkable claims is under about a
quarter, `sde_cascade` is a code linter that needs no model and should be built as
one.

This is the same move as `athlete_matching/measure_residue.py`, which took entity
alignment off the map: local, no API key, no network, free to re-run, and the number
decides rather than the intuition.

    python sde_cascade/inventory.py              # the measurement
    python sde_cascade/inventory.py --show jev   # read the claims in one bucket
    python sde_cascade/inventory.py --selftest   # classifier rules, no corpus

## What counts as a claim

A claim is a statement about the state of the world that a later session could act on
and be wrong about. Instructions ("run the backfill with ..."), recommendations and
open questions are NOT claims - nothing about them can be stale. They are separated
out first and reported, not silently dropped, because "we write mostly instructions"
would itself change what `sde_cascade` should be.

## The five buckets

    code        a date, count, path, SHA, test result, or "X exists" - `stat`, `git`,
                a rerun or a file read settles it. No model.
    jev         prose asserting what a NAMED OTHER DOCUMENT says or records. This is
                `citation_check`'s exact shape and the only bucket Jev is needed for.
    causal      "X because Y", "the cause is Z" - neither code nor a Noul settles a
                causal claim; it needs a controlled measurement. The 09-20 "the band
                is the bibliography" error was one of these.
    instruction imperative or prohibition. Not a state claim.
    opinion     recommendation, judgement, hedge, or an open question.

Order matters and is deliberate: instruction and opinion are tested BEFORE the claim
buckets, so "run `git log` to check the SHA" is an instruction rather than a code
claim. Then causal, then jev, then code. Anything with a causal connective is causal
even if it also cites a number, because the number is not what makes it wrong.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import random
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

DEV = Path(r"C:\Users\eric_rash\Desktop\DEV")
SEED = 20260920          # fixed so the sample is reproducible and not shopped for
SAMPLE_SIZE = 10

# Holding areas and worktrees are not the live corpus.
EXCLUDE = ("_to_delete", ".claude/worktrees", "/_ARCHIVE/")


# --- what a claim looks like -------------------------------------------------

# Imperative openers and prohibitions. Checked first: a sentence telling the next
# session what to do is not a statement about state, however many paths it names.
INSTRUCTION = re.compile(
    r"^(?:run|use|check|set|add|remove|delete|open|read|write|copy|move|edit|"
    r"rotate|register|disable|enable|re-?run|verify|confirm|pull|push|merge|"
    r"install|build|start|stop|never|do not|don't|always|avoid|keep|put|make)\b"
    r"|^(?:.{0,40}\b(?:must|should|needs? to|has to)\b)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

# Recommendations, judgements, hedges, and questions.
OPINION = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:recommend|recommended|suggest|worth doing|worth it|probably|likely|"
    r"seems|appears to be|arguably|prefer|better to|consider|maybe|perhaps|"
    r"unclear|not sure|open question|decide|decision|TBD|\?$)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

# Causal and explanatory connectives. A causal claim is wrong in a way no single
# lookup catches - it needs an experiment.
CAUSAL = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:because|since it|due to|caused by|the cause|that is why|which is why|"
    r"the reason|as a result|therefore|so that|leads to|results in|explains why|"
    r"is what makes|stems from)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

# A reference to another document: a path, a PR/issue number, a named .md, a skill.
DOC_REFERENCE = re.compile(
    r"(?:`[^`]*\.(?:md|json|ps1|py|sh|bat|yml|yaml|toml|txt)[^`]*`"
    r"|\b(?:PR|pull request|issue)\s*#?\d+"
    r"|\b[\w./-]+\.md\b"
    r"|\bSTATUS\.md\b|\bCLAUDE\.md\b|\bAGENTS\.md\b|\bhandoff\b)",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

# Verbs that make a statement be ABOUT what a document asserts.
SAYING_VERB = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:says?|said|states?|records?|recorded|documents?|documented|notes?|noted|"
    r"asserts?|claims?|describes?|reports?|reported|lists?|listed|names?|named|"
    r"mentions?|specifies|indicates?|per|according to|calls? for|flags?|"
    r"carries|carry|carried)\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

# Things a machine can settle on its own.
CODE_EVIDENCE = re.compile(
    r"\b\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\b"                      # a date
    r"|\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b"                        # a git SHA
    r"|\b\d[\d,.]*\s*(?:%|GB|MB|KB|ms|s\b|files?|rows?|lines?|entries|entry|"
    r"tests?|errors?|repos?|commits?|sessions?|records?|nodes?|edges?|passed|"
    r"failed|skills?|pages?|claims?)"             # a count with a unit
    r"|\bexit(?:s|ed)?\s*(?:code\s*)?\d+"         # an exit code
    r"|\b(?:exists?|missing|absent|present|installed|registered|enabled|disabled|"
    r"gitignored|untracked|tracked|clean|dirty|merged|pushed|staged)\b"
    r"|`[^`]+`",                                  # any literal path/command/value
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

BUCKETS = ("code", "jev", "causal", "instruction", "opinion")


def classify(text: str) -> str:
    """One claim, one bucket. Order is the design - see the module docstring."""
    stripped = text.strip()
    if INSTRUCTION.search(stripped):
        return "instruction"
    if OPINION.search(stripped):
        return "opinion"
    if CAUSAL.search(stripped):
        return "causal"
    if DOC_REFERENCE.search(stripped) and SAYING_VERB.search(stripped):
        return "jev"
    if CODE_EVIDENCE.search(stripped):
        return "code"
    return "opinion"          # no evidence of any kind: prose, not a state claim


# --- pulling claims out of a handoff -----------------------------------------

FENCE = re.compile(r"^\s*```")
HEADING = re.compile(r"^\s*#")
BULLET = re.compile(r"^\s*[-*+]\s+(.*)$")
TABLE = re.compile(r"^\s*\|")


def strip_markdown(text: str) -> str:
    text = re.sub(r"\*\*([^*]*)\*\*", r"\1", text)
    text = re.sub(r"~~([^~]*)~~", r"\1", text)
    text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", text)
    return text.strip()


def claims_in(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Bullets and prose sentences. Headings, fences and tables are skipped.

    Tables are skipped deliberately and it is a real limit: a table row is usually a
    dense code-checkable claim, so excluding them if anything UNDERSTATES the code
    share. Said here rather than discovered later.
    """
    out: list[str] = []
    in_fence = False
    for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        if FENCE.match(raw):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            continue
        if in_fence or HEADING.match(raw) or TABLE.match(raw) or not raw.strip():
            continue
        bullet = BULLET.match(raw)
        body = strip_markdown(bullet.group(1) if bullet else raw)
        if not body:
            continue
        if bullet:
            out.append(body)
        else:
            for sentence in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+(?=[A-Z`*])", body):
                sentence = sentence.strip()
                if len(sentence) > 25:
                    out.append(sentence)
    return [c for c in out if len(c) > 15]


def sample_handoffs(n: int = SAMPLE_SIZE) -> list[Path]:
    found = [
        p for p in DEV.rglob("*.md")
        if "handoffs" in p.parts and not any(x in p.as_posix() for x in EXCLUDE)
    ]
    found.sort()                                  # rglob order is not stable
    random.Random(SEED).shuffle(found)
    return found[:n]


# --- the measurement ---------------------------------------------------------

def run(show: str | None) -> int:
    handoffs = sample_handoffs()
    if not handoffs:
        print("no handoffs found", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1

    tally = {b: [] for b in BUCKETS}
    per_file = []
    for path in handoffs:
        claims = claims_in(path)
        counts = {b: 0 for b in BUCKETS}
        for claim in claims:
            bucket = classify(claim)
            tally[bucket].append((path, claim))
            counts[bucket] += 1
        per_file.append((path, len(claims), counts))

    print(f"sde_cascade scoping inventory - seed {SEED}, {len(handoffs)} handoffs\n")
    print(f"{'handoff':<58} {'all':>4} {'code':>5} {'jev':>4} {'caus':>5} "
          f"{'instr':>6} {'opin':>5}")
    print("-" * 92)
    for path, total, counts in per_file:
        label = path.relative_to(DEV).as_posix()
        if len(label) > 56:
            label = "..." + label[-53:]
        print(f"{label:<58} {total:>4} {counts['code']:>5} {counts['jev']:>4} "
              f"{counts['causal']:>5} {counts['instruction']:>6} "
              f"{counts['opinion']:>5}")

    total = sum(len(v) for v in tally.values())
    print("-" * 92)
    print(f"{'TOTAL':<58} {total:>4} " + " ".join(
        f"{len(tally[b]):>{w}}" for b, w in
        zip(("code", "jev", "causal", "instruction", "opinion"), (5, 4, 5, 6, 5))))

    # The pre-registered rule is about CHECKABLE claims, so instructions and
    # opinions come out of the denominator. They are reported above because their
    # size is itself a finding.
    checkable = len(tally["code"]) + len(tally["jev"]) + len(tally["causal"])
    print(f"\nstatements extracted        {total}")
    print(f"  not state claims          {len(tally['instruction']) + len(tally['opinion'])}"
          f"  (instructions + opinions/questions)")
    print(f"  checkable claims          {checkable}")
    if checkable:
        for bucket, who in (("code", "code settles it"),
                            ("jev", "needs a model"),
                            ("causal", "needs a measurement")):
            share = 100 * len(tally[bucket]) / checkable
            print(f"    {bucket:<10} {len(tally[bucket]):>4}  {share:5.1f}%  {who}")
        jev_share = 100 * len(tally["jev"]) / checkable
        print(f"\nPRE-REGISTERED RULE: under ~25% Jev-shaped -> build it as a code "
              f"linter, no model.")
        print(f"MEASURED: {jev_share:.1f}% Jev-shaped -> "
              + ("CODE LINTER" if jev_share < 25 else "JEV BUILD IS JUSTIFIED"))

    if show:
        print(f"\n--- every claim in bucket '{show}' ---")
        for path, claim in tally.get(show, []):
            print(f"  [{path.parent.parent.parent.name}] {claim[:150]}")
    return 0


def selftest() -> int:
    """The classifier's rules, on hand-written lines. No corpus, no network."""
    cases = [
        # (text, expected bucket, why this case exists)
        ("`perch.duckdb` last written 2026-04-30.", "code",
         "a date on a named file - stat settles it"),
        ("The backup manifest holds 125 entries.", "code",
         "a count with a unit"),
        ("Tests: gps_report/tests 112 passed.", "code",
         "a test result - rerunning settles it"),
        ("`_INBOX/docs/STATUS.md` records perch.duckdb as 2026-04-30.", "jev",
         "asserts what another document says - citation_check's shape"),
        ("The handoff states that PRs #7 and #8 were merged.", "jev",
         "doc reference plus a saying verb"),
        ("The band is 37 because the paper has 37 references.", "causal",
         "causal connective - no lookup settles it, it needed an experiment"),
        ("Never run the backfill through `pull.sh`.", "instruction",
         "prohibition, not a state claim"),
        ("Run tests with `.venv/bin/python -m pytest`.", "instruction",
         "imperative even though it names a path"),
        ("Windows must stop writing to the database.", "instruction",
         "obligation, not a statement about current state"),
        ("Recommend naming Windows the Perch owner.", "opinion",
         "a recommendation cannot be stale"),
        ("Which machine owns forceplate.db?", "opinion",
         "an open question is not a claim"),
        ("Run `git log` to check the SHA on 2026-09-19.", "instruction",
         "ORDER MATTERS: instruction beats the date that follows it"),
        ("STATUS.md says the run failed because the disk was full.", "causal",
         "ORDER MATTERS: causal beats the document reference"),
    ]
    failures = 0
    for text, expected, why in cases:
        got = classify(text)
        ok = got == expected
        failures += not ok
        print(f"  [{'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}] {expected:<11} "
              f"{'' if ok else '(got ' + got + ') '}{text[:58]:<60} {why}")
    print(f"\n{len(cases) - failures} of {len(cases)} classifier cases pass")
    return 1 if failures else 0


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--selftest", action="store_true",
                        help="classifier rules only; no corpus, no network")
    parser.add_argument("--show", choices=BUCKETS,
                        help="print every claim landing in one bucket")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    return selftest() if args.selftest else run(args.show)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

def claims_in(path: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Bullets and prose sentences. Headings, fences and tables are skipped.

    Lines are REFLOWED into blocks first. These files are hard-wrapped at about 90
    characters, so reading each physical line as a unit shreds sentences mid-clause -
    the first run produced fragments like "The question was not 'who is good' but 'is
    there any structure in the" as standalone claims, which inflated the count and
    classified noise. A block is a bullet plus its indented continuations, or a run
    of consecutive prose lines; only then is it split on sentence boundaries.

    Tables are skipped deliberately and it is a real limit: a table row is usually a
    dense code-checkable claim, so excluding them if anything UNDERSTATES the code
    share. Said here rather than discovered later.
    """
    blocks: list[str] = []
    current: list[str] = []

    def flush() -> None:
        if current:
            blocks.append(" ".join(current))
            current.clear()

    in_fence = False
    for raw in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
        if FENCE.match(raw):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            flush()
            continue
        if in_fence or HEADING.match(raw) or TABLE.match(raw) or not raw.strip():
            flush()
            continue
        bullet = BULLET.match(raw)
        if bullet:
            flush()                       # a new bullet ends the previous block
            current.append(bullet.group(1).strip())
        else:
            current.append(raw.strip())   # continuation or prose, same block
    flush()

    out: list[str] = []
    for block in blocks:
        body = strip_markdown(block)
        if not body:
            continue
        for sentence in re.split(r"(?<=[.!?])\s+(?=[A-Z`*\"'(])", body):
            sentence = sentence.strip()
            if len(sentence) > 15:
                out.append(sentence)
    return out

# What the linter would actually have to check. "Build a code linter" is not a
    # spec; this is. Each row is a claim shape with a one-line mechanism, ranked by
    # how often it occurs in the corpus, so the build order comes out of the data
    # rather than out of taste. A claim can match more than one shape.
    shapes = (
        ("a literal path / command / value", re.compile(r"`[^`]+`"),
         "resolve the path, or re-run the command"),
        ("a count with a unit", re.compile(
            r"\b\d[\d,.]*\s*(?:%|GB|MB|KB|ms|files?|rows?|lines?|entries|tests?|"
            r"errors?|repos?|commits?|sessions?|records?|nodes?|edges?|skills?)",
            re.IGNORECASE), "recount from the source"),
        ("a date", re.compile(r"\b\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\b"), "stat / git log"),
        ("a git SHA", re.compile(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b"), "git cat-file -e"),
        ("an existence / status word", re.compile(
            r"\b(?:exists?|missing|absent|present|installed|registered|enabled|"
            r"disabled|gitignored|untracked|tracked|merged|pushed)\b",
            re.IGNORECASE), "a file test, git, or the scheduler"),
        ("a pass / fail result", re.compile(
            r"\b(?:passed|failed|exit(?:s|ed)?\s*(?:code\s*)?\d+|0 errors)\b",
            re.IGNORECASE), "re-run the suite"),
    )
    print("\nWhat the linter would check, ranked by how often the shape occurs")
    print(f"  (over the {len(tally['code'])} code-checkable claims; "
          f"a claim can match several)")
    counted = [(name, sum(bool(rx.search(c)) for _, c in tally["code"]), how)
               for name, rx, how in shapes]
    for name, count, how in sorted(counted, key=lambda r: -r[1]):

        print(f"\n--- every claim in bucket '{show}' ---")
        for path, claim in tally.get(show, []):
            print(f"  [{path.parent.parent.parent.name}] {claim[:150]}")
    return 0

input.content:
# `sde_cascade` — scoped, measured, and the answer is: build it without Jev

`sde_cascade` was ranked **first** on the re-ranked capability map on 2026-09-20. The
map did not rank it for building, it ranked it for **measuring**, and it pre-registered
the rule before any code existed:

> If the Jev-shaped share of checkable claims is under about a quarter, `sde_cascade`
> is a code linter that needs no model and should be built as one.

Measured: **7.7%**. The answer is a code linter.

This is the fourth time a measurement has moved an item down the map, after entity
alignment (withdrawn), PP_Recruiting screening (rejected) and the Zotero renames
(skipped). It is the second time the *deliverable was the measurement rather than the
build* — `athlete_matching/measure_residue.py` is the precedent, and this follows it
deliberately: local, no key, no network, free to re-run.

Code: `sde_cascade/inventory.py`.

```
python sde_cascade/inventory.py               # the measurement
python sde_cascade/inventory.py --selftest    # 20 cases, no corpus, no network
python sde_cascade/inventory.py --lint-paths  # the top check, run for real
python sde_cascade/inventory.py --show jev    # read any bucket
```

## The measurement

Ten handoffs, sampled with a fixed seed from the 79 in `~/DEV` (worktrees, `_ARCHIVE`
and `_to_delete` excluded), 583 statements extracted.

| bucket | n | share of checkable | who settles it |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **code** | 252 | **88.4%** | `stat`, `git`, a file test, a re-run |
| **jev** | 22 | **7.7%** | a model — `citation_check`'s exact shape |
| **causal** | 11 | 3.9% | neither; needs a controlled measurement |
| instruction | 28 | — | not a state claim |
| opinion / question | 22 | — | not a state claim |
| unclassified | 248 | — | excluded from the denominator |

**7.7% Jev-shaped against a pre-registered 25% threshold.** Not a close call.

### The result survives the adversarial reading

248 statements landed unclassified, which is the obvious place for a missed Jev claim
to hide, and eyeballing a bucket is not evidence. So the script bounds it: assume
**every** unclassified statement that so much as mentions a document or uses a saying
verb is secretly Jev-shaped, and move all 30 of them across.

**52 / 315 = 16.5% — still a code linter.** The decision does not depend on the
classifier being right at the margin.

## Two defects in the classifier, found by auditing it rather than trusting it

Both were caught by reading the buckets after the first run, and both had been
biasing the answer **toward** the conclusion it was already leaning at — which is the
direction that should worry you most.

1. **Markdown hard-wrapping shredded prose.** These files wrap at about 90
   characters, and the extractor read each physical line as a claim, producing
   fragments like *"The question was not 'who is good' but 'is there any structure in
   the"* as standalone statements. Lines are now reflowed into blocks before
   sentence-splitting.
2. **The document-reference rule was too narrow.** It required a file extension or a
   PR number, so *"This is recorded in ADR 0013."* — a textbook Jev-shaped claim —
   was missed entirely. Widening it moved the Jev share from 4.5% to 7.7%.

A third change was structural: the fallback used to be `opinion`, which quietly
swelled that bucket to 46% of everything and hid real claims inside it. **A fallback
that lands in a real bucket is a fallback nobody audits.** It is now a named
`unclassified` bucket, counted and excluded.

## What the linter should actually check

"Build a code linter" is not a spec. This is, ranked by how often each shape occurs
across the 252 code-checkable claims (a claim can match several):

| claim shape | n | share | mechanism |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| a literal path / command / value | 214 | **84.9%** | resolve the path, or re-run the command |
| an existence / status word | 39 | 15.5% | a file test, `git`, or the scheduler |
| a git SHA | 32 | 12.7% | `git cat-file -e` |
| a count with a unit | 27 | 10.7% | recount from the source |
| a date | 23 | 9.1% | `stat` / `git log` |
| a pass / fail result | 2 | 0.8% | re-run the suite |

One check covers 85% of the surface: **does every backticked path in a handoff still
resolve?** Start there and stop; the rest is a long tail.

## The prototype, and why the real work is false alarms

`--lint-paths` runs that top check for real over the same ten handoffs. The first run
reported **43%** of path literals unresolved. That number was mostly wrong, and
walking it down is the finding:

| fix | unresolved |
|---|---:|
| first run | 43% |
| skip URLs and elided `...` literals; map `~/DEV/` to the Windows layout | 34% |
| resolve cross-repo references against every project in `~/DEV` | 28% |
| skip Mac-only vault paths; handle the `DEV/` root prefix | **24%** |

**Not one additional file was found. Every point came from removing a false alarm.**
The classes, each of which was a real misfire and not a hypothesis:

- **`~/DEV/...` is the Mac layout.** On this box DEV lives under `Desktop`, so the
  same handoff line is correct on one machine and unresolvable on the other.
- **Cross-repo references are the common case, not the corner case.** A handoff in

> is a code linter that needs no model and should be built as one.

Measured: **7.7%**. The answer is a code linter.

This is the fourth time a measurement has moved an item down the map, after entity
alignment (withdrawn), PP_Recruiting screening (rejected) and the Zotero renames
(skipped). It is the second time the *deliverable was the measurement rather than the
build* — `athlete_matching/measure_residue.py` is the precedent, and this follows it
deliberately: local, no key, no network, free to re-run.

Code: `sde_cascade/inventory.py`.

python sde_cascade/inventory.py --selftest    # 20 cases, no corpus, no network
python sde_cascade/inventory.py --lint-paths  # the top check, run for real
python sde_cascade/inventory.py --show jev    # read any bucket
```

## The measurement

Ten handoffs, sampled with a fixed seed from the 79 in `~/DEV` (worktrees, `_ARCHIVE`
and `_to_delete` excluded), 583 statements extracted.

| bucket | n | share of checkable | who settles it |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **code** | 252 | **88.4%** | `stat`, `git`, a file test, a re-run |
| **jev** | 22 | **7.7%** | a model — `citation_check`'s exact shape |
| **causal** | 11 | 3.9% | neither; needs a controlled measurement |
| instruction | 28 | — | not a state claim |
| opinion / question | 22 | — | not a state claim |
| unclassified | 248 | — | excluded from the denominator |

**7.7% Jev-shaped against a pre-registered 25% threshold.** Not a close call.

### The result survives the adversarial reading

248 statements landed unclassified, which is the obvious place for a missed Jev claim
to hide, and eyeballing a bucket is not evidence. So the script bounds it: assume
**every** unclassified statement that so much as mentions a document or uses a saying
verb is secretly Jev-shaped, and move all 30 of them across.

classifier being right at the margin.

   fragments like *"The question was not 'who is good' but 'is there any structure in
   the"* as standalone statements. Lines are now reflowed into blocks before

| a count with a unit | 27 | 10.7% | recount from the source |
| a date | 23 | 9.1% | `stat` / `git log` |
| a pass / fail result | 2 | 0.8% | re-run the suite |

The map ranked `sde_cascade` **first** and pre-registered the rule rather than the answer:

> under about a quarter Jev-shaped → it is a code linter that needs no model.

**Measured: 7.7%.** Not a close call.

## The measurement

Ten handoffs, fixed seed, from the 79 in `~/DEV`. 583 statements.

| bucket | n | share of checkable | who settles it |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **code** | 252 | **88.4%** | `stat`, `git`, a file test, a re-run |
| **jev** | 22 | **7.7%** | a model — `citation_check`'s exact shape |
| causal | 11 | 3.9% | neither; needs a controlled measurement |

**It survives the adversarial reading.** 248 statements landed unclassified — the obvious place for a missed Jev claim to hide, and eyeballing a bucket is not evidence. So assume **every** unclassified statement that so much as mentions a document or uses a saying verb is secretly Jev-shaped: **52/315 = 16.5%, still a code linter.** The decision does not depend on the classifier being right at the margin.

## Two defects in my own classifier

Both found by reading the buckets rather than trusting the total, and **both had biased the answer toward the conclusion it was already leaning at** — the direction that should worry you most.

1. **Markdown hard-wrapping shredded prose** into mid-clause fragments like *"…but is there any structure in the"*. Lines are now reflowed before sentence-splitting.
2. **The document-reference rule was too narrow** — it required an extension or a PR number, so *"This is recorded in ADR 0013"* was missed entirely. That is the Jev-shaped claim exactly. Widening it moved 4.5% → 7.7%.

Structural fix: the fallback used to be `opinion`, which swelled that bucket to 46% and hid real claims in it. **A fallback that lands in a real bucket is a fallback nobody audits.** Now named, counted, excluded.

## The spec, from the data

| claim shape | n | share | mechanism |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| a literal path / command / value | 214 | **84.9%** | resolve it, or re-run it |
| an existence / status word | 39 | 15.5% | file test, `git`, scheduler |
| a git SHA | 32 | 12.7% | `git cat-file -e` |
| a count with a unit | 27 | 10.7% | recount from source |
| a date | 23 | 9.1% | `stat` / `git log` |

One check covers 85%: **does every backticked path still resolve?**

## The prototype, and why the real work is false alarms

`--lint-paths` runs that check for real. First run said 43% unresolved. That number was mostly wrong:

| fix | unresolved |
|---|---:|
| first run | 43% |
| skip URLs and elided `...`; map `~/DEV/` to the Windows layout | 34% |
| resolve cross-repo references against every project | 28% |
| skip Mac-only vault paths; handle the `DEV/` root prefix | **24%** |

**Not one additional file was found — every point came from removing a false alarm.** `~/DEV/` is the *Mac* layout; cross-repo references are the common case; `github.com/erash11/…` is a URL with no scheme; the SecondBrain vault is Mac-only.

The lesson for whoever builds this: **a cross-machine linter has to know the layout of both boxes, or it reports the difference between them as rot.** A checker shipping at 43% noise gets switched off in a week.

Residual 24% are **leads, not defects**. Spot-checked: `~/DEV/Website` genuinely moved and `output/_ledger.md` is genuinely absent, while `gps_history.duckdb` was a false alarm now fixed.

## Verification

`python sde_cascade/inventory.py --selftest` → **20 cases**, no key, no network. Verifier suites unaffected and still green (17/17, 12/12).

Fourth item measurement has moved down the map, after entity alignment, PP_Recruiting and the Zotero renames.

def sample_handoffs(n: int = SAMPLE_SIZE, seed: int = SEED) -> list[Path]:
    found = [
        p for p in DEV.rglob("*.md")
        if "handoffs" in p.parts and not any(x in p.as_posix() for x in EXCLUDE)
    ]
    found.sort()                                  # rglob order is not stable
    random.Random(seed).shuffle(found)
    return found[:n]


# The individual evidence alternatives, so the code bucket can be taken apart the
# same way the unclassified one was. The last alternative of CODE_EVIDENCE is a bare
# backtick, which means ANY quoted token lands a sentence in `code` - "the `project`
# skill handles ranking" included. That inflates the denominator, and a bound that
# only ever moves claims INTO jev would never notice.
DATED = re.compile(r"\b\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\b")
SHA = re.compile(r"\b[0-9a-f]{7,40}\b")
COUNTED = re.compile(
    r"\b\d[\d,.]*\s*(?:%|GB|MB|KB|ms|files?|rows?|lines?|entries|tests?|errors?|"
    r"repos?|commits?|sessions?|records?|nodes?|edges?|skills?|pages?|claims?)",
    re.IGNORECASE)
STATUSY = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:exists?|missing|absent|present|installed|registered|enabled|disabled|"
    r"gitignored|untracked|tracked|merged|pushed|passed|failed)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
BACKTICKED = re.compile(r"`([^`]+)`")


def backtick_only(claim: str) -> bool:
    """Its ONLY evidence is a quoted token - no date, SHA, count or status word."""
    return bool(BACKTICKED.search(claim)) and not (
        DATED.search(claim) or SHA.search(claim)
        or COUNTED.search(claim) or STATUSY.search(claim))


def has_path_literal(claim: str) -> bool:
    """Carries at least one backticked token that is actually path-shaped."""
    for raw in BACKTICKED.findall(claim):
        literal = raw.strip().rstrip(".,;:")
        if (PATH_LITERAL.match(literal) and "..." not in literal
                and not URL_LIKE.search(literal)
                and not any(ch in literal for ch in "*?<>|$ ")):
            return True
    return False

# The individual evidence alternatives, so the code bucket can be taken apart the
# same way the unclassified one was. The last alternative of CODE_EVIDENCE is a bare
# backtick, which means ANY quoted token lands a sentence in `code` - "the `project`
# skill handles ranking" included. That inflates the denominator, and a bound that
# only ever moves claims INTO jev would never notice.

    r"\b\d[\d,.]*\s*(?:%|GB|MB|KB|ms|files?|rows?|lines?|entries|tests?|errors?|"
    r"repos?|commits?|sessions?|records?|nodes?|edges?|skills?|pages?|claims?)",
    re.IGNORECASE)
STATUSY = re.compile(
    r"\b(?:exists?|missing|absent|present|installed|registered|enabled|disabled|"
    r"gitignored|untracked|tracked|merged|pushed|passed|failed)\b", re.IGNORECASE)
BACKTICKED = re.compile(r"`([^`]+)`")


def backtick_only(claim: str) -> bool:
    """Its ONLY evidence is a quoted token - no date, SHA, count or status word."""
    return bool(BACKTICKED.search(claim)) and not (
        DATED.search(claim) or SHA.search(claim)
        or COUNTED.search(claim) or STATUSY.search(claim))

        if (PATH_LITERAL.match(literal) and "..." not in literal
                and not URL_LIKE.search(literal)
                and not any(ch in literal for ch in "*?<>|$ ")):

    return False

### How hard the result was pushed, in both directions

A bound that only ever moves claims *into* Jev flatters the conclusion, so both ends
are bounded.

**Bound A, the numerator.** 248 statements landed unclassified — the obvious place
for a missed Jev claim to hide, and eyeballing a bucket is not evidence. Assume
**every** unclassified statement that so much as mentions a document or uses a saying
verb is secretly Jev-shaped: **16.5%.**

**Bound B, the denominator.** The code bucket is inflated by construction — the last
alternative of its rule is a bare backtick, so *any* quoted token qualifies, and "the
`project` skill handles ranking" counts as code. Drop every code claim whose only
evidence is a non-path quoted token (74 of 252): **10.4%.**

**Both at once — the number the conclusion has to survive: 21.6%.**

### And the seed is measured, not assumed

An earlier draft of this file asserted that a different seed "would not move 7.7% to
25%". That is exactly the unmeasured claim this project's rule exists to stop, so

| 20260920 | 285 | 7.7% | 16.5% | 10.4% | 21.6% |

| 777 | 274 | 10.2% | 20.1% | 15.3% | **28.6%** |

also holds under either bound alone, on every seed. But stacking **both** adversarial
readings at once lands at 21.6–29.9%, and **2 of 4 seeds cross the threshold**.

reading is deliberately unreasonable (it assumes every ambiguous statement is

# `sde_cascade` — scoped, measured, and the answer is: build it without Jev

`sde_cascade` was ranked **first** on the re-ranked capability map on 2026-09-20. The
map did not rank it for building, it ranked it for **measuring**, and it pre-registered
the rule before any code existed:

> If the Jev-shaped share of checkable claims is under about a quarter, `sde_cascade`
> is a code linter that needs no model and should be built as one.

Measured: **7.7%**. The answer is a code linter.

This is the fourth time a measurement has moved an item down the map, after entity
alignment (withdrawn), PP_Recruiting screening (rejected) and the Zotero renames
(skipped). It is the second time the *deliverable was the measurement rather than the
build* — `athlete_matching/measure_residue.py` is the precedent, and this follows it
deliberately: local, no key, no network, free to re-run.

Code: `sde_cascade/inventory.py`.

```
python sde_cascade/inventory.py               # the measurement
python sde_cascade/inventory.py --selftest    # 20 cases, no corpus, no network
python sde_cascade/inventory.py --lint-paths  # the top check, run for real
python sde_cascade/inventory.py --show jev    # read any bucket
```

## The measurement

Ten handoffs, sampled with a fixed seed from the 79 in `~/DEV` (worktrees, `_ARCHIVE`
and `_to_delete` excluded), 583 statements extracted.

| bucket | n | share of checkable | who settles it |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **code** | 252 | **88.4%** | `stat`, `git`, a file test, a re-run |
| **jev** | 22 | **7.7%** | a model — `citation_check`'s exact shape |
| **causal** | 11 | 3.9% | neither; needs a controlled measurement |
| instruction | 28 | — | not a state claim |
| opinion / question | 22 | — | not a state claim |
| unclassified | 248 | — | excluded from the denominator |

**7.7% Jev-shaped against a pre-registered 25% threshold.** Not a close call.

### The result survives the adversarial reading

248 statements landed unclassified, which is the obvious place for a missed Jev claim
to hide, and eyeballing a bucket is not evidence. So the script bounds it: assume
**every** unclassified statement that so much as mentions a document or uses a saying
verb is secretly Jev-shaped, and move all 30 of them across.

**52 / 315 = 16.5% — still a code linter.** The decision does not depend on the
classifier being right at the margin.

## Two defects in the classifier, found by auditing it rather than trusting it

Both were caught by reading the buckets after the first run, and both had been
biasing the answer **toward** the conclusion it was already leaning at — which is the
direction that should worry you most.

1. **Markdown hard-wrapping shredded prose.** These files wrap at about 90
   characters, and the extractor read each physical line as a claim, producing
   fragments like *"The question was not 'who is good' but 'is there any structure in
   the"* as standalone statements. Lines are now reflowed into blocks before
   sentence-splitting.
2. **The document-reference rule was too narrow.** It required a file extension or a
   PR number, so *"This is recorded in ADR 0013."* — a textbook Jev-shaped claim —
   was missed entirely. Widening it moved the Jev share from 4.5% to 7.7%.

A third change was structural: the fallback used to be `opinion`, which quietly
swelled that bucket to 46% of everything and hid real claims inside it. **A fallback
that lands in a real bucket is a fallback nobody audits.** It is now a named
`unclassified` bucket, counted and excluded.

## What the linter should actually check

"Build a code linter" is not a spec. This is, ranked by how often each shape occurs
across the 252 code-checkable claims (a claim can match several):

| claim shape | n | share | mechanism |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| a literal path / command / value | 214 | **84.9%** | resolve the path, or re-run the command |
| an existence / status word | 39 | 15.5% | a file test, `git`, or the scheduler |
| a git SHA | 32 | 12.7% | `git cat-file -e` |
| a count with a unit | 27 | 10.7% | recount from the source |
| a date | 23 | 9.1% | `stat` / `git log` |
| a pass / fail result | 2 | 0.8% | re-run the suite |

One check covers 85% of the surface: **does every backticked path in a handoff still
resolve?** Start there and stop; the rest is a long tail.

## The prototype, and why the real work is false alarms

`--lint-paths` runs that top check for real over the same ten handoffs. The first run
reported **43%** of path literals unresolved. That number was mostly wrong, and
walking it down is the finding:

| fix | unresolved |
|---|---:|
| first run | 43% |
| skip URLs and elided `...` literals; map `~/DEV/` to the Windows layout | 34% |
| resolve cross-repo references against every project in `~/DEV` | 28% |
| skip Mac-only vault paths; handle the `DEV/` root prefix | **24%** |

**Not one additional file was found. Every point came from removing a false alarm.**
The classes, each of which was a real misfire and not a hypothesis:

- **`~/DEV/...` is the Mac layout.** On this box DEV lives under `Desktop`, so the
  same handoff line is correct on one machine and unresolvable on the other.
- **Cross-repo references are the common case, not the corner case.** A handoff in
  `claude-global-memory` names `gps_report/data/gps_history.duckdb`, which lives in
  `DataBase_GPS_Reporting`. Resolving only against the handoff's own repo called an
  existing file missing.
- **`github.com/erash11/S2_Evaluation` is a URL** with no scheme, so it satisfies any
  reasonable path pattern.
- **The SecondBrain vault is Mac-only** — already an open item in
  `_INBOX/docs/STATUS.md` — so every `Knowledge/...` note a handoff cites is
  unresolvable here and is not stale.

That is the engineering lesson for whoever builds this: **a cross-machine linter has
to know the layout of both boxes, or it reports the difference between them as rot.**
A checker shipping at 43% noise gets switched off in a week, and the deliverable
verifier's whole credibility came from having zero false alarms.

The residual 24% are **leads, not defects** — a handoff may name a file since renamed
or deliberately deleted. Spot-checked: `~/DEV/Website` genuinely moved,
`S2_Evaluation/output/_ledger.md` and `data/ol_scores.csv` are genuinely absent, while
`gps_history.duckdb` was a false alarm now fixed.

## What this means for the map

- **`sde_cascade` comes off the Jev list.** It is real work with a real surface — 126
  `STATUS.md` files and 79 handoffs — but it is a script, not a model. Build it as
  `--lint-paths` grown up: a pre-commit or closeout check that resolves paths, SHAs
  and dates and prints leads.
- **The 7.7% does not disappear**, it just does not justify a build of its own. Those
  22 claims are `citation_check`'s exact shape, and the verifier already exists. If
  the linter ever wants them, point the existing machinery at a handoff instead of a
  deck rather than writing anything new.
- **The causal bucket is the interesting one.** Eleven claims that neither code nor a
  Noul can settle — "the band is the bibliography" was one, and it sent a session's
  top-priority task at the wrong layer. Nothing on the capability map addresses these,
  and no tool will; they need someone to run the experiment. Worth knowing they are
  about 4% of what a handoff asserts.

## Honest limits

- **Ten handoffs, one seed.** Re-running with a different seed would move the
  percentages; it would not move 7.7% to 25%.
- **Tables are skipped** by the extractor. A table row is usually a dense
  code-checkable claim, so this if anything understates the code share.
- **The classifier is heuristic and I wrote both it and the test cases.** The
  adversarial bound exists precisely because that is not independent verification.
  The bucket dumps are there so the judgement can be checked rather than trusted:
  `--show code`, `--show jev`, `--show unclassified`.

# `sde_cascade` — scoped, measured, and the answer is: build it without Jev

`sde_cascade` was ranked **first** on the re-ranked capability map on 2026-09-20. The
map did not rank it for building, it ranked it for **measuring**, and it pre-registered
the rule before any code existed:

> If the Jev-shaped share of checkable claims is under about a quarter, `sde_cascade`
> is a code linter that needs no model and should be built as one.

Measured: **7.7%**. The answer is a code linter.

This is the fourth time a measurement has moved an item down the map, after entity
alignment (withdrawn), PP_Recruiting screening (rejected) and the Zotero renames
(skipped). It is the second time the *deliverable was the measurement rather than the
build* — `athlete_matching/measure_residue.py` is the precedent, and this follows it
deliberately: local, no key, no network, free to re-run.

Code: `sde_cascade/inventory.py`.

```
python sde_cascade/inventory.py               # the measurement
python sde_cascade/inventory.py --selftest    # 20 cases, no corpus, no network
python sde_cascade/inventory.py --lint-paths  # the top check, run for real
python sde_cascade/inventory.py --show jev    # read any bucket
```

## The measurement

Ten handoffs, sampled with a fixed seed from the 79 in `~/DEV` (worktrees, `_ARCHIVE`
and `_to_delete` excluded), 583 statements extracted.

| bucket | n | share of checkable | who settles it |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| **code** | 252 | **88.4%** | `stat`, `git`, a file test, a re-run |
| **jev** | 22 | **7.7%** | a model — `citation_check`'s exact shape |
| **causal** | 11 | 3.9% | neither; needs a controlled measurement |
| instruction | 28 | — | not a state claim |
| opinion / question | 22 | — | not a state claim |
| unclassified | 248 | — | excluded from the denominator |

**7.7% Jev-shaped against a pre-registered 25% threshold.**

### How hard the result was pushed, in both directions

A bound that only ever moves claims *into* Jev flatters the conclusion, so both ends
are bounded.

**Bound A, the numerator.** 248 statements landed unclassified — the obvious place
for a missed Jev claim to hide, and eyeballing a bucket is not evidence. Assume
**every** unclassified statement that so much as mentions a document or uses a saying
verb is secretly Jev-shaped: **16.5%.**

**Bound B, the denominator.** The code bucket is inflated by construction — the last
alternative of its rule is a bare backtick, so *any* quoted token qualifies, and "the
`project` skill handles ranking" counts as code. Drop every code claim whose only
evidence is a non-path quoted token (74 of 252): **10.4%.**

**Both at once — the number the conclusion has to survive: 21.6%.**

### And the seed is measured, not assumed

An earlier draft of this file asserted that a different seed "would not move 7.7% to
25%". That is exactly the unmeasured claim this project's rule exists to stop, so
`--sweep` measures it over four samples:

| seed | claims | measured | bound A | bound B | A and B |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 20260920 | 285 | 7.7% | 16.5% | 10.4% | 21.6% |
| 1 | 288 | 10.8% | 21.2% | 16.1% | **29.9%** |
| 42 | 347 | 8.4% | 16.8% | 12.0% | 23.2% |
| 777 | 274 | 10.2% | 20.1% | 15.3% | **28.6%** |

**The measured share is stable at 7.7–10.8% and never comes near 25%.** The decision
also holds under either bound alone, on every seed. But stacking **both** adversarial
readings at once lands at 21.6–29.9%, and **2 of 4 seeds cross the threshold**.

So the honest statement is narrower than the first draft of this document claimed:
**`sde_cascade` is a code linter on the measured share and on either bound alone —
but "not a close call" is not a claim this data supports.** The double-adversarial
reading is deliberately unreasonable (it assumes every ambiguous statement is
Jev-shaped *and* strips a third of the code bucket), and it is still worth knowing
that is where the line sits.

## Two defects in the classifier, found by auditing it rather than trusting it

Both were caught by reading the buckets after the first run, and both had been
biasing the answer **toward** the conclusion it was already leaning at — which is the
direction that should worry you most.

1. **Markdown hard-wrapping shredded prose.** These files wrap at about 90
   characters, and the extractor read each physical line as a claim, producing
   fragments like *"The question was not 'who is good' but 'is there any structure in
   the"* as standalone statements. Lines are now reflowed into blocks before
   sentence-splitting.
2. **The document-reference rule was too narrow.** It required a file extension or a
   PR number, so *"This is recorded in ADR 0013."* — a textbook Jev-shaped claim —
   was missed entirely. Widening it moved the Jev share from 4.5% to 7.7%.

A third change was structural: the fallback used to be `opinion`, which quietly
swelled that bucket to 46% of everything and hid real claims inside it. **A fallback
that lands in a real bucket is a fallback nobody audits.** It is now a named
`unclassified` bucket, counted and excluded.

## What the linter should actually check

"Build a code linter" is not a spec. This is, ranked by how often each shape occurs
across the 252 code-checkable claims (a claim can match several):

| claim shape | n | share | mechanism |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| a literal path / command / value | 214 | **84.9%** | resolve the path, or re-run the command |
| an existence / status word | 39 | 15.5% | a file test, `git`, or the scheduler |
| a git SHA | 32 | 12.7% | `git cat-file -e` |
| a count with a unit | 27 | 10.7% | recount from the source |
| a date | 23 | 9.1% | `stat` / `git log` |
| a pass / fail result | 2 | 0.8% | re-run the suite |

One check covers 85% of the surface: **does every backticked path in a handoff still
resolve?** Start there and stop; the rest is a long tail.

## The prototype, and why the real work is false alarms

`--lint-paths` runs that top check for real over the same ten handoffs. The first run
reported **43%** of path literals unresolved. That number was mostly wrong, and
walking it down is the finding:

| fix | unresolved |
|---|---:|
| first run | 43% |
| skip URLs and elided `...` literals; map `~/DEV/` to the Windows layout | 34% |
| resolve cross-repo references against every project in `~/DEV` | 28% |
| skip Mac-only vault paths; handle the `DEV/` root prefix | **24%** |

**Not one additional file was found. Every point came from removing a false alarm.**
The classes, each of which was a real misfire and not a hypothesis:

- **`~/DEV/...` is the Mac layout.** On this box DEV lives under `Desktop`, so the
  same handoff line is correct on one machine and unresolvable on the other.
- **Cross-repo references are the common case, not the corner case.** A handoff in
  `claude-global-memory` names `gps_report/data/gps_history.duckdb`, which lives in
  `DataBase_GPS_Reporting`. Resolving only against the handoff's own repo called an
  existing file missing.
- **`github.com/erash11/S2_Evaluation` is a URL** with no scheme, so it satisfies any
  reasonable path pattern.
- **The SecondBrain vault is Mac-only** — already an open item in
  `_INBOX/docs/STATUS.md` — so every `Knowledge/...` note a handoff cites is
  unresolvable here and is not stale.

That is the engineering lesson for whoever builds this: **a cross-machine linter has
to know the layout of both boxes, or it reports the difference between them as rot.**
A checker shipping at 43% noise gets switched off in a week, and the deliverable
verifier's whole credibility came from having zero false alarms.

The residual 24% are **leads, not defects** — a handoff may name a file since renamed
or deliberately deleted. Spot-checked: `~/DEV/Website` genuinely moved,
`S2_Evaluation/output/_ledger.md` and `data/ol_scores.csv` are genuinely absent, while
`gps_history.duckdb` was a false alarm now fixed.

## What this means for the map

- **`sde_cascade` comes off the Jev list.** It is real work with a real surface — 126
  `STATUS.md` files and 79 handoffs — but it is a script, not a model. Build it as
  `--lint-paths` grown up: a pre-commit or closeout check that resolves paths, SHAs
  and dates and prints leads.
- **The 7.7% does not disappear**, it just does not justify a build of its own. Those
  22 claims are `citation_check`'s exact shape, and the verifier already exists. If
  the linter ever wants them, point the existing machinery at a handoff instead of a
  deck rather than writing anything new.
- **The causal bucket is the interesting one.** Eleven claims that neither code nor a
  Noul can settle — "the band is the bibliography" was one, and it sent a session's
  top-priority task at the wrong layer. Nothing on the capability map addresses these,
  and no tool will; they need someone to run the experiment. Worth knowing they are
  about 4% of what a handoff asserts.

## Honest limits

- **Ten handoffs, one seed.** Re-running with a different seed would move the
  percentages; it would not move 7.7% to 25%.
- **Tables are skipped** by the extractor. A table row is usually a dense
  code-checkable claim, so this if anything understates the code share.
- **The classifier is heuristic and I wrote both it and the test cases.** The
  adversarial bound exists precisely because that is not independent verification.
  The bucket dumps are there so the judgement can be checked rather than trusted:
  `--show code`, `--show jev`, `--show unclassified`.

Bound the denominator too, and measure the seed instead of asserting it

Review caught that the adversarial bound only ran one direction. It moved ambiguous
statements INTO jev but never asked whether the code bucket was inflated - and it is,
by construction: the last alternative of CODE_EVIDENCE is a bare backtick, so any
quoted token lands a sentence in `code`, "the `project` skill handles ranking"
included. A bound that only flatters the conclusion is not a bound.

Bound B drops the code claims whose only evidence is a non-path quoted token (74 of
252) and gives 10.4%. Both bounds stacked give 21.6%. And the seed, which an earlier
draft asserted "would not move 7.7% to 25%", is now measured over four samples:

  seed        claims  measured  bound A  bound B  A and B
  20260920       285      7.7%    16.5%    10.4%    21.6%
  1              288     10.8%    21.2%    16.1%    29.9%
  42             347      8.4%    16.8%    12.0%    23.2%
  777            274     10.2%    20.1%    15.3%    28.6%

The measured share is stable at 7.7-10.8% and never approaches 25%, and the call
holds under either bound alone on every seed. But both at once lands at 21.6-29.9%
and crosses the threshold on 2 of 4 samples. So the conclusion stands and the
rhetoric does not: "not a close call" has been removed from every document.

Second correction: "one check covers 85%" conflated two different sets. 84.9% of code
claims carry a backticked token; only 39.3% carry a literal that is actually
path-shaped and resolvable. The top check is still the right place to start, at about
two fifths of the surface rather than five sixths.

Also pins the reflow bug that was found by reading output rather than by a test:
three cases covering a hard-wrapped sentence extracting as one claim, two sentences on
one line still splitting, and a bullet ending the previous block. Corpus discovery is
cached so a four-seed sweep does not walk 39k files four times.

23 selftest cases, was 20. Verifier suites unaffected and still green.

So I don't think "what do we build next" is the live question. One conversation unblocks both. That's the highest-leverage move available and it isn't one I can make.

=== README ===
# TOS brief source papers - Zotero import kit

The deliverable verifier checks a claim against the SOURCE PAPER. None of the
TOS evidence brief's sources are in the Zotero library - searched by author, DOI
and title, zero hits - so the brief cannot be verified against its sources until
they are imported.

**Claude cannot do this step, but it is now one command for Eric.**

The Zotero *web* key on this machine is read-only (`write: false` in `zotero_health`).
With Zotero **open**, a second path appears that the key has nothing to do with: the
connector endpoint the browser extension uses. Verified live - `/connector/ping`
returns 200 with `supportsAttachmentUpload: true`. So Zotero running does change the
situation.

What it does not change is Claude's own permissions: a POST to a local service is
refused as an External System Write. So the import is scripted and left to be run:

```
! python verifier/tos_sources/import_to_zotero.py --go
```

Dry-run it first (no flag) to see what it would fetch - that half is tested and
returns all four records. Add `--all` for the full 109.

## The four that matter first

These are the papers behind the three known misquotes and the statistical fix.
Import these and the verifier can be pointed at the brief's central claims.

| PMID | Why |
|---|---|
| `40673787` | Kamarajugadda - misquote 1: exceedance rate read as volume composition |
| `36003968` | Takaba - misquote 2: 53% increase described as 'roughly doubles' |
| `39844736` | Ulman - misquote 3: 49.9% variance misattributed to LE screening |
